title: Run the car park on the clock it is given

blocks.text: A car park's barrier controller prints a ticket at the entry, gives every car 15 free minutes, and lets drivers pay for more time at a machine. The team wants to test the night-shift rules without waiting for the night, so the controller now hands `CarPark` the `Clock` it runs on, and the tests hand it one they move by hand.

items: `enter(...)`: the ticket printed when a car drives in;
`overstayed(...)`: whether the car has stayed past the time its ticket covers;
`pay(...)`: the ticket after the driver pays for more time.

blocks.text: When you're done, every time `CarPark` uses is the time of the clock it was built with, and a driver who pays is covered for the extra time. About four lines in total.

cases.says: a new ticket carries the plate and covers 15 minutes from its time of entry
the time of entry on a ticket is the car park's clock time, not the machine's
a car counts as overstayed once the car park's clock passes the time its ticket covers
the ticket returned after paying covers the extra time

origin.section: Code That Needs the Current Time Takes a Clock

concepts: Code that needs the current time takes a Clock and calls now(clock), so a test fixes or moves the instant and the zone.
java.time values are immutable: plusDays, with and the like return a new value, so a dropped result changes nothing, and javac does not warn.
